_about: Graphics quality tiers (lane TIERS, rebased 2026-11-05 on the v73 project). A tier = the HDRP asset of the QualitySettings level with the same name (Low / Medium / High / Ultra, each level -> its own HDRP_<Tier>.asset, Ultra = HDRP_Max.asset) + the 'flags' overlay below, which uses the runtime_flags.json schema (RuntimeQuality.Flags) plus ssaoQuality, bloomQuality, motionBlur, asyncCompute, particleScale, lodBiasMul. Every tier lists ALL managed keys, so a tier switch never leaves a stale value. The baseTier (ultra) is never overlaid: runtime_flags.json is its definition (the approved look, QC keeps tuning that one file) and every switch re-clones the authored volume profiles; low / medium / high are presets that overlay runtime_flags.json (their values win for the keys they list). Quality numbers: 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high. Selection order: -quality:<tier> arg > PlayerPrefs[prefsKey] (ignored in harness runs: balance / verify / proofs / perfbench always use defaultTier) > defaultTier. Menu / UI: read GameSettings (Scripts/GameSettings.cs), never this file directly.
_ultra: ULTRA IS THE APPROVED v69 LOOK. Every Ultra flag is either the same value as runtime_flags.json (clouds, volumetricFog, ssgi, ssr, ssao, contactShadows, shadows, renderScale 67, ssgiQuality 2, ssgiFullRes, fogQuality 2, cascades 2, hideMHHead) or the value already authored in HDRP/Global.asset (ssrQuality 1, ssaoQuality 1, bloomQuality 1, motionBlur 0.05, shadowDistance 40) so that switching back to Ultra at runtime restores exactly what the scene was authored with. exposure is NOT a tier key: look.json exposure is the one exposure (the old exposureEV key is gone). lodBiasMul multiplies crack_flicker.json lodBias (2.0 today); 1.0 = unchanged. python -I _agents/laneTIERS/check_tiers.py diffs Ultra against runtime_flags.json, Global.asset and hdrp_lighting_ultra.json.
_targets: NOT MEASURED. Low / Medium / High are meant for 8-16 GB discrete GPUs at 30-60 fps (1080p output, STP upscale); minVramMb only feeds GameSettings.SuggestedTier() (the 'recommended' label). The default stays ultra: Dom wants MAX graphics unless the player picks lower.
